candidate.title: PAIR
candidate.scope: The PAIR middle row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: sequence-directed PNA/CPP/Bpa capture of RNA-binding proteins in living cells, followed by magnetic capture and SDS-PAGE protein visualization. PAIR expands to peptide nucleic acid (PNA)-assisted identification of RNA-binding proteins. TIVA (top row) and CLaP (bottom row) are neighboring, separately labelled workflows, not alternative PAIR branches or additional targets of this card. The matched collection page is headed PAIR and reproduces this architecture; its unshown RNA-sequencing claim and associated kit do not add a library-preparation branch. Scope is the schematic, not an assertion that all PAIR implementations share every preparation detail.

unknowns.question: What molecular ligand bridges the photoactivated PNA/protein adduct to the orange strand-bearing magnetic beads, and does this interface require removal of RNA before capture? The supplied PAIR image shows the transition but the supplied Bell abstract does not resolve it. An accessible primary PAIR methods passage or figure describing the bead interface and any RNA handling is needed to name that chemistry.

The matched secondary collection paragraph says RNA strands are sequenced and proteins can be reverse-crosslinked, whereas the assigned PAIR row ends at SDS-PAGE and the supplied primary abstract does not establish those downstream claims. Primary implementation evidence would be needed before interpreting them as part of a PAIR RNA-sequencing architecture; they are outside this depicted route.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the extraction at the declared PAIR schematic scope. All in-scope transformations and the released-CPP branch are represented, and all material/data routes agree with their receiving operations. The probe/RNP association and bead capture are genuine joint interfaces; CPP release produces two components of one cleavage event. No independent workflows have been collapsed. The diagram supports protein capture and visualization, without a depicted sequencing library. The two expressly limited unknowns do not prevent this schematic-level account; no source correction is required by the supplied primary abstract.
